body:
# the contributor audit of the exact three-probability support frontier

Source: `candidate 98dc66551a701077`.


The dual AM-GM bound uses 4 eta_j eta_k>=P_i row by row. In the
reciprocal-triangle regime, eta_i=sqrt(P_1P_2P_3)/(2P_i) satisfies all
three constraints with equality. With H=sum eta_i, its claimed matrix
Z_ij=(H/2-eta_i)/eta_j is nonnegative exactly when 2eta_i<=H, has
column sums one, and gives row value H-2eta_i. Hence the total objective
attains H=e2/(2sqrt(e3)). Equality in a reciprocal-triangle inequality
is included and merely makes one row zero.

If the inequality at i fails, P_i<P_jP_k/(P_j+P_k). The displayed
eta triple satisfies two constraints with equality and the remaining
one strictly. The proposed two-row matrix has column-i allocations
P_j/(P_j+P_k), P_k/(P_j+P_k), and the other two columns are forced.
It attains sqrt(P_j+P_k), exactly the dual sum. At most one reciprocal
triangle inequality can fail. Compactness and continuous dependence of
the objective handle zero probabilities without claiming a nonexistent
strictly positive optimizer.

I also read the full coordinate-face support proof in
`candidate df39f37487bbac05`.
Mass outside the active rows can be moved to an active off-diagonal
recipient when at least two active rows remain. Generalized Holder
and identical optimizing probability columns give the exact attained
identity h_3(P_i^(1/3),0)=h_2(sqrt(P_i))^(2/3). Thus every pair sum at
least one really pays, whether or not the three-row interior formula
applies.

For actual probabilities (a,1-b,c), all remaining pair sums below one
give a,c<b and a+c<1. Setting s=a+c, t=1-b gives e2=ac+st and e3=act.
The two roots of e2^2-4e3 are ac/(1+sqrt(1-s))^2 and
ac/(1-sqrt(1-s))^2. The reciprocal triangle inequality at t gives
t>=ac/s, strictly above the lower root. Therefore only the upper root
is the relevant frontier in this regime. This ordering, positivity
before squaring, and the separate boundary formula prevent the spurious
small-t branch from being counted as payment.

No actual same-centroid geometry proving that the remaining probabilities
cross this frontier is asserted. The new scalar centroid constraints
F>C and F(1-F)<C do not suffice by themselves: a=c=2/5, b=49/100,
C=1/4 satisfy them strictly, whereas P=(2/5,51/100,2/5) is in the
reciprocal-triangle regime and e2^2-4e3=-59/15625<0. This last tuple is
only a counterexample to a scalar relaxation, not an actual geometric
configuration or an OC counterexample.
